Sordid

SOR-did -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, SOR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Sordid is involving immoral actions or motives.

Voters were shocked by the sordid details of the senator's secret land deals.

Worked Example

The biography reveals that the beloved tycoon built his fortune by bribing officials, blackmailing rivals, and quietly ruining anyone who threatened to talk.

A fortune built on bribery and blackmail has a sordid history. Sordid describes actions and motives stained by immorality -- conduct so dishonorable it feels dirty just to examine.

How Sordid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

corrupt

corrupt: acting dishonestly for personal gain

disgraceful

disgraceful: bringing shame or dishonor

seedy

seedy: disreputable and run-down

Antonyms

honorable

honorable: morally upright

admirable

admirable: deserving respect and approval

How Strong Is It? — seedy → sordid → vile

seedy vs. sordid

seedy vs. sordid: Seedy is gentler than sordid -- a seedy motel just looks run-down and slightly suspicious, while sordid means the immoral behavior is real, not just an appearance.

vile vs. sordid

vile vs. sordid: Vile goes further than sordid: a sordid scheme is dishonest and shameful, but a vile one is so morally repulsive that almost anyone who hears about it is disgusted.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — sord-

root — sord-: dirt, filth (Latin sordes)

suffix — -id

suffix — -id: having the quality of (Latin -idus)

Put it together

Put it together: Sordid comes from Latin sordes, 'dirt, filth,' via sordidus, 'dirty, shabby.' English borrowed the literal grime and turned it moral: sordid actions are morally filthy -- conduct that leaves a smudge on everyone who touches it.

Use the root in a new word: squalid

Use the root in a new word: squalid: The inspectors condemned the squalid apartment block, where paint peeled and pipes leaked in every unit.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Sordid clings to conduct and motives: a sordid past, sordid dealings, the sordid details of a scandal. It judges behavior as morally dirty -- greed, betrayal, exploitation. For content that offends the senses or public decency -- crude language, indecent images -- obscene is the word instead.
